chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Al-Qasim ibn Urwa, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, from his father, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Whoever sits in a gathering wherein an Imam from the Imams is insulted, despite being able to stand up and leave, but he does not do so, Allah will clothe him in disgrace in the world, and punish him in the Hereafter, and strip him of the good of what He bestowed upon him from our recognition.

key_terms.مَعْرِفَتِنَا: Our recognition (spiritual knowledge of the Imams)

ai.seo_question: What is the consequence of sitting silently while an Imam is insulted?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith establishes 'al-ghiybah' (absence) as a mandatory act of reverence, distinguishing between mere physical presence and active endorsement of the Imams' dishonor. The chain of narration highlights the transmission of this principle through key companions, emphasizing that neglecting this duty when capable results in the forfeiture of 'ma'rifah' (spiritual recognition), which is central to Shia identity. This serves as a practical guideline for maintaining communal integrity and individual spiritual standing in the face of societal disrespect toward the Ahl al-Bayt.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from his father, from Al Qasim Bin Urwa, from Ubeyd Bin Zurara, from his father, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The one who sits in a gathering wherein an Imam<sup>asws</sup> from the Imams<sup>asws</sup> is insulted despite being able upon the walking away, but he does not do so, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Clothe him in disgrace in the world and Punish him in the Hereafter, and Confiscate what he had been Favoured with upon him, from our<sup>asws</sup> recognition’.
en.sarwar: 15. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from his father from al-Qasim ibn ‘Urwah from ‘Ubayd ibn Zurara from his father from abu Ja’far (a.s.) who has said the following: “

Whoever sits in a gathering where any of A ’immah is abused and one is able to move out of such gathering, but does not do so, Allah will dress him with humiliation in this world and punish him in the next life and take away from him the goodness that was granted to him due to his acquaintance with us.’”
